London, 14<sup>th</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**The proposed transaction** involving platinum companies Impala, Mvela and Northam have been called off because of ongoing volatility in platinum prices and the current global economic uncertainty, the companies said in a joint statement on Wednesday.  Announcing the withdrawal of the November 19 cautionary announcement, the companies said that agreement on exchange ratios for the implementation of the proposed transaction could not be reached.  “Negotiations have therefore been terminated,” Implats, Mvela and Northam said.  Although the three acknowledged that the near-term outlook for the platinum sector remains challenging, they stated that they continue to believe in the long-term fundamentals of the industry. 

_Source:  Impala Platinum/Mining Weekly_ 

**Northam Platinum** is forging ahead with the Booysendal project despite the failed overture from Impala Platinum that foundered on a disagreement over the price.  “We are certainly not pulling the plug on Booysendal. It’s not only our future but a chance to expand production with cheaper ounces,” Northam CEO Glyn Lewis said.  Northam is cash flow positive after working capital and expects to remain neutral in coming months based on forecasts the company’s management was hearing, he said. The company is debt free.  Lewis declined to say how much cash was on Northam’s books, but said funding the bankable study into Booysendal, which should be completed by year end, was not an issue. 

Last year Mvela was talking of a R7bn capital cost for Booysendal so that it could produce 430,000 PGM oz/year over a 30-year life. A modular approach could reduce that cost substantially.  Northam has spoken of a modular approach, building 120,000 tonnes/month declines and scaling up the number of shafts as market circumstances dictate.  “We are continuing with the bankable study. It is going to be dependent on the financial circumstances prevailing towards the end of the year; everyone’s forecasting it to improve. We are doing the mine design to take into account all aspects,” Lewis said. 

There has long been speculation that Aquarius Platinum would be a logical partner on the deeper portions of Booysendal, accessing them through its contiguous Everest South infrastructure. The question now is whether Aquarius will approach or be approached now that Impala has walked away. Aquarius has shut its Everest South after rock instability shut a shaft for at least six months. Whether Aquarius has the financial capacity to become involved in Booysendal will have to be seen. _Source:  Mining Mx_ 

**The Detroit 3** automakers have pulled out of this year’s Tokyo auto show to cut costs.  Ford Motor Co. confirmed Japanese media reports that Ford would not be participating this year.  Exhibiting in the show, which is held every two years, cost General Motors $2 million in 2007. That’s money better spent elsewhere, said Rick Brown, president of

GM Asia Pacific.  “We won’t be participating,” Brown said today. Chrysler made the same decision, based on “ the current challenges and market situation…(and) in order to secure limited resources invested efficiently on activities necessary to sustain our business”, said a spokesman.  The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association is debating whether to cancel the event. A number of non-American companies dropped out of this month’s Detroit auto show, including Nissan Motor Co., Suzuki Motor Corp., Porsche AG, Rolls-Royce and Land Rover. Mitsubishi Motors Corp. cancelled its corporate presence, but local Mitsubishi dealers put together an exhibit. _Source:  Automotive News_
